meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лушать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to listen', paired with 'послушать'.

examples.text: Слушай, Самсон, я тут подумал. Твой начальник — такой опытный специалист.
examples.trans: Listen, Samson, I've been thinking. Your boss is such an experienced specialist.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'here', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: There's someone here to see you.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

подумать.gloss: to think (for a while), to think it over

meanings.en: to think (for a while), to think it over
meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'умать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to think (for a while), to think it over', paired with 'думать'.

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'счёт').

examples.text: Не волнуйся ты насчёт этого Мишкина.
examples.trans: Don't you worry about that Mishkin.

examples.text: Не волнуйся ты насчёт этого Мишкина. Работаем мы с ним.
examples.trans: Don't you worry about that Mishkin. We're working on him.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'our, ours', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'bet, wager, dispute' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This is a bet, wager, dispute.
I will definitely win this bet.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'правый'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('wrong, mistaken').

examples.trans: You are wrong in this argument.

examples.text: Был неправ. Простите. Я хочу закончить начатое.
examples.trans: I was wrong. Forgive me. I want to finish what I started.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?
And this is for you. A toy car!

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('right').

examples.text: Заходите. Поставьте, пожалуйста, правую ногу на кровать.
examples.trans: Come in. Please put your right foot on the bed.

examples.text: Поставьте, пожалуйста, правую ногу на кровать.
examples.trans: Please put your right foot on the bed.

examples.text: Я тебя обманул, и ты был прав. Теперь всё изменилось, Самсон.
examples.trans: I tricked you, and you were right. Now everything has changed, Samson.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'yes, indeed', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'all right, OK', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, that; it is', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'порить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to argue, to dispute', paired with 'поспорить'.

examples.trans: That's a nightmare, I don't argue.

examples.text: Это кошмар, я не спорю. Но зачем на видео снимать?
examples.trans: That's a nightmare, I don't argue. But why film it on video?

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'for the sake of', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Work, work. It's all for us.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'пулярный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('popular').

examples.trans: Our restaurant is very popular right now.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, into', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but; so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'so, then; like that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you?
So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

examples.text: Разговорчики, лейтенант Соколов! Быстро на рабочее место.
examples.trans: That's enough talk, Lieutenant Sokolov! Back to your desk, quickly.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'огласиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to agree', paired with 'соглашаться'.

examples.trans: Admit it / Don't you agree, that's much better.

examples.text: Это гораздо лучше, чем двенадцать лет. Согласитесь?
examples.trans: That's much better than twelve years. Don't you agree?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'with', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: Prefix 'раз-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'говаривать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to talk, to speak'.

examples.trans: Why are you talking so rudely?

examples.text: А что вы так грубо разговариваете?
examples.trans: Why are you talking so rudely?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian expressive spoken interjection meaning 'uh-huh, yeah', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Yeah, right, like with the Cayenne?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'too, also', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы же здесь выросли. И о людях тоже надо думать.
examples.trans: After all, we grew up here. And you have to think about people too.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'can, to be able', paired with 'смочь'.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'верять'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to check, test, verify', paired with 'проверить'.

examples.trans: You think he is testing us?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'даться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to surrender, to give up', paired with 'сдаваться'.

examples.trans: Raise your hands and surrender to the authorities.

examples.text: Тогда я, пожалуй, сдамся прямо сразу.
examples.trans: Then I think I will surrender right away.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
